observation: A main-thread sample on ./target/release/echarts list --format json spent most of its time in _dyld_start, which means dynamic-loader/process startup dominates the wall-clock sample.

recommendation: Keep the wall-clock CLI benchmark, but split the report into startup floor and command work.
Measure a same-runtime no-op control first, then measure the real CLI command, and compare within the same runtime/build on the same host.
If you need CLI-internal logic only, instrument from main/subcommand entry or use a profiler/tracer that separates _dyld_start and loader time from handler time.
notes: Using /bin/echo as a universal baseline is too optimistic; it does not pay the same loader/runtime cost as node or the Rust binary.
For this environment, a fairer interpretation is that most observed wall-clock time is startup/environment cost, not subcommand logic.
The current full multi-case benchmark script was stopped because the startup floor makes exhaustive serial sampling too slow to finish in a useful time.
